jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
**Job Class:** GIS Analyst

**FLSA Status:** Non Exempt

**Effective Date:** August 2026


**Definition**

  

Performs a variety of professional level work in the analysis, design, programming, testing, and maintenance of the District’s Geographical Information System (GIS); creates and maintains databases; and produces a variety of maps and graphical presentations by manual and automated means.


**Distinguishing Characteristics**


This is a journey level classification, fully competent to independently perform a variety of specialized technical duties related to the development, planning, designing, organizing and maintenance of the District’s GIS. Incumbents are expected to be familiar with a diverse set of procedures and situations. Employees at this level receive only occasional instruction, assistance or direction as new or unusual situations arise and are fully aware of the District’s operating procedures and policies.


**Examples of Essential Duties**


The following duties are typical for this classification. Depending upon the assignment, the employee may not perform all of the listed duties and may be required to perform additional or different duties from those below to address business needs and changing business practices. Management retains the right to add, remove, or change duties at any time.




* Oversees the District’s Enterprise GIS platform including maintaining updated water and land facilities; performs quality control on data download processes; and manipulates data from outside sources for use in the GIS.
* Analyzes data and prepares associated reports/maps for use by appropriate department.
* Recommends and assists in the implementation of GIS goals and objectives; works to establish schedules and methods related to the use of AutoCAD and GIS Standards.
* Implements and develops procedures for use of GIS functionalities; prepares related protocols and provides training to a variety of GIS users.
* Plans, prioritizes, assigns, supervises, and ensures accuracy of the work of staff involved in duties supporting the District’s GIS system and mapping functions.
* Manages the GIS division’s budget, including preparation and administration; preparing cost estimates; submitting justifications for staffing, equipment, and supplies; monitors and controls expenditures.
* Participates in the selection of staff; and provides or coordinates staff training in the uses and operations of GIS applications.
* Prepares written protocols for difficult and complex GIS system and database usage, including troubleshooting protocols.
* Coordinates and integrates GIS functions with other departments, other agencies/jurisdictions, engineers, developers and the public.
* Prepares requests for proposals (RFPs) for GIS services and products. Assists with the selection of outside vendors and consultants. Provides oversight and direction to outside vendors and consultants and monitors their performance.
* Analyzes, reviews, modifies, and ensures accuracy of complex mapping and data requests utilizing required spatial and/or GIS tools; performs scripting and/or programming.
* Coordinates with Information Technology (IT) Department to ensure network connections to GIS server; make related recommendations.
* Designs and/or modifies GIS programming as necessary to accommodate the needs of a variety of users; verifies accuracy of digitized data to ensure accuracy and quality of automated information.
* Provides advanced technical support to end users.
* Maintains regular attendance and adheres to prescribed work schedule to conduct job responsibilities.
* Builds and maintains positive working relationships with coworkers, other District employees and the public using principles of good customer service.
* Performs related duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

***Knowledge of:***

* Basic mapping and civil engineering (reading and interpreting records drawings/plans).
* GIS system concepts and analytical techniques, including computer mapping and digital data conversion, manipulation and analysis
* Basic operating principles, parameters, methods, practices and limitations of computer platforms and networks.
* Principles and practices of systems analysis and design applicable to GIS programs.
* Application development methods, tools and utilities applicable to the GIS system.
* Object\-oriented programming languages (e.g., Java scripting, Python).
* CAD principles, techniques, equipment and software.
* Principles and applications of GIS, GPS and other engineering software, including ESRI\-based GIS software and its applications and related programming languages.
* Postgres, MS SQL Server and other database applications.
* Modern office methods, procedures, and equipment including common office computer software and database programs, including the Microsoft Suite of Programs (Word, Excel, Outlook, Access, and PowerPoint).
* Principles and practices of supervision, training, and performance evaluation.
* Principles and practices of budget preparation and monitoring.
* Principles and practices of project management and contract administration.
* Principles and practices of good customer service and work safety.
* Techniques and principles of effective interpersonal communication.
* English usage, spelling, grammar and punctuation.




***Ability To:***

* Plan, prioritize, organize, implement and direct staff assigned to support the District’s GIS system and perform mapping functions.
* Collect, interpret, and integrate geographic and facilities data from multiple sources.
* Read, interpret and analyze record maps, construction drawings, graphs, satellite and aerial images and geographic conditions; perform spatial analysis and other related data used for mapping and design.
* Understand, use and apply relational database management systems, tools, and techniques.
* Diagnose, research, and resolve problems with GIS databases, applications, software and hardwar

jobs.title: Project Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
:
**GFT** is seeking a **Project Environmental Scientist** to join our growing Environmental Practice! This role follows a hybrid work model, requiring regular attendance at either our **Berkeley, CA or Roseville, CA** offices.  

GFT’s Environmental team delivers integrated planning, permitting, and compliance solutions that support infrastructure development across North America. With more than 140 professionals in 22 offices, the team guides clients through NEPA and permitting processes, ecological and regulatory assessments, and environmental remediation efforts. Their expertise spans transportation, power, water, and facilities markets — working alongside agencies at federal, state, and local levels. From stream restoration to complex regulatory requirements and advance critical infrastructure projects. **What you’ll be challenged to do:**
This is an excellent career opportunity for an experienced, motivated Project Environmental Scientist who is ready to take the next step in their career. We are looking for someone how combines strong technical permitting expertise – a professional that enjoys doing the work, working directly with clients and regulatory agencies and helping to building a growing environmental practice.
The successful candidate will have strong working knowledge of California and federal environmental permitting requirements, particularly as they apply to transportation, water and power projects. This individual will lead and prepare permit applications and technical documentation, coordinate with regulatory agencies, manage permitting assignments and support projects through planning and through design and construction. **In this capacity, the successful candidate will be responsible for the following:*** Lead and support natural resource analysis and environmental permitting for transportation, water, and other infrastructure projects throughout California.
* Develop permitting strategies and identify federal, state, and local regulatory requirements during project planning, CEQA/NEPA and design.
* Prepare and manage permit applications and supporting technical documentation, including Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements, and other applicable federal, state, and local permits and approvals.
* Coordinate directly with regulatory agencies, including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Boards, California Department of Fish and Wildlife, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, NOAA Fisheries, and other agencies as appropriate.
* Conduct wetland delineations, jurisdictional assessments, biological field studies, and other technical investigations necessary to support project permitting as well as CEQA/NEPA analysis.
* Author and review technical reports, CEQA/NEPA analysis, permit applications, environmental commitments, mitigation plans, and related environmental deliverables.
* Work closely with engineering and design teams to identify natural resource and permitting constraints, develop practical avoidance and minimization measures, and incorporate environmental requirements into project design and construction.
* Support environmental compliance during construction, including implementation and tracking of permit conditions and mitigation commitments.
* Manage environmental permitting assignments, including scope, schedule, budget, staffing, deliverables, and client communications.
* Contribute to and increasingly lead environmental components of proposals, interviews, scopes of work, and cost estimates.
* Contribute to the continued development of GFT’s California Environmental Practice.


:
**What you will bring to our firm:*** Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology, the physical sciences, or closely related field.
* Approximately 5\-8 years of progressively responsible experience, with significant experience delivering natural resources and permitting services for infrastructure projects.
* Demonstrated experience preparing and managing environmental permits for projects in California.
* Strong working knowledge of applicable federal and California environmental regulations.
* Experience working with and developing relationships with regulatory agencies such as USACE, CDFW, RWQCB, USFWA and/or NOAA Fisheries.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Self\-starter, able to complete tasks with minimal supervision and direction.
* Willingness to travel and execute work in a variety of settings and environmental conditions (heat, cold, rain, etc.).
* Demonstrated leadership and interpersonal skills to work effectively with others and achieve results.
* Demonstrated agility working with multi\-disciplined infrastructure projects.
* Demonstrated professional judgment, consistency, strong attention to detail, and background of high\-quality work products.
* Ability to prepare and deliver presentations and lead meetings, when needed.
* An entrepreneurial mindset and interest in helping grow a developing California environmental practice.

**What we prefer you bring:*** A Master’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology or a closely related field.
* Established relationships with California transportation agencies, water agencies, municipalities, regulatory agencies, or other infrastructure clients.
* Experience with Caltrans, local transportation agencies, passenger rail/transit agencies, water districts, utilities, or similar California public\-sector clients.
* GIS experience.
* Relevant professional certifications or specialized permitting/natural\-resource credentials.

### **Compensation:**


The salary range for this role is **$95,000 \- $135,000**; Salary is dependent upon experience and geographic location.### **Featured Benefits:**

* Hybrid (in\-person and remote) work environment.

jobs.title: Environmental Geologist/Engineer/Scientist
jobs.description:
Do you like working with different project teams in a fast\-paced environment? Are you interested in joining an organization focused on making a positive impact? If so, we'd like to talk with you about growing with us.


We are looking for a Staff Geologist, Engineer, or Scientist to join our Long Beach/Los Angeles, California team. We are EnSafe Inc., an employee\-owned, global professional services firm.



As an Environmental Geologist/Engineer/Scientist, you will work in an environment that fosters creativity, collaboration at all levels, a culture of support, and professional growth. EnSafe emphasizes empowering staff to practice our profession passionately and without limitations.



EnSafe's philosophy is to seek individuals with extraordinary talent and to keep them at the forefront of emerging technologies through continuing professional development. Our employees are outgoing, initiative\-taking, and thrive in a fast\-paced consulting environment. EnSafe offers competitive salaries and benefits, an outstanding work environment, and the opportunity to work on innovative and exciting projects.


**DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES**  

***In this role, you will:***


* Perform Phase I/II environmental site assessments
* Prepare work plans
* Conduct site investigation activities (sampling of soil, groundwater, surface water, indoor air, vapor intrusion, soil gas, drinking water, and building materials)
* Provide environmental compliance support to senior regulatory specialists, including data collection for permitting and/or registration; regulatory compliance evaluation and assessment; and preparation of plans and reports.
* Field documentation
* Assisting in authoring technical reports


**SKILLS/EXPERIENCE**  

***Minimum Skills and Requirements:***


* Requires a minimum of a BS (MS preferred) in Geology, Engineering, or other Science.
* 0\-2 years of experience (previous internships are helpful)
* Professional registration, certification, GID, geotechnical, and/or geophysics experience are a plus.
* Preferred: EIT, PE, PG, and the ability to obtain a PE/PG license in other states.
* Outstanding proficiency in Microsoft programs, including Word and Excel
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Regional travel likely
* Occasional weekend work is required.


**Why Join EnSafe?**


* **Employee\-Owned Advantage**  

EnSafe is 100% employee\-owned, with an ESOP (Employee Stock Ownership Plan) since 1997\. That means when EnSafe succeeds, you succeed too, turning company growth directly into shared rewards.
* **Commitment to Growth and Wellness**  

The company supports personalized career development, mentorship, and employee wellness initiatives such as health tracking tools.
* **Purpose‑Driven Work**  

EnSafe's mission focuses on impactful environmental, health, and safety consulting—making a real difference in communities and is backed by its long\-standing technical credibility.
* **Safety as a Value, Not Just a Service**  

Safety is deeply embedded in our culture, prioritizing employee well\-being in addition to helping clients maintain compliance. We stress that *"safety is part of everything we do."*
* **A Culture of Freedom \& Ownership**  

At EnSafe, our career philosophy is built on freedom. The freedom to take initiative, achieve your goals, and shape your own career path Employees are encouraged to pursue growth in a flexible, entrepreneurial environment.
* **Challenging, Creative Work**  

Workdays at EnSafe are anything but ordinary, fast\-paced, dynamic, and filled with opportunities to tackle projects in environmental consulting, health \& safety, engineering, and technology. Every day calls for creativity, innovation, and agile problem\-solving.

  


**\#LI\-MR1**

**About EnSafe**



EnSafe began as a two\-person firm in 1980, navigating complex regulatory compliance issues on behalf of our clients. We nurture our people with growth and development opportunities. We build enduring, trustful relationships with each of our clients, with a focus on high ethical and safety standards. We build this reputation by attracting high\-quality people and retaining them for the long term.



At EnSafe, we are dedicated to fostering a diverse and authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles at our company.



EnSafe is committed to being an EEO employer and all qualified candidates will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, citizenship, age (except for bona fide occupational qualifications), sex, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, military or veteran status, any other status protected by federal, state, or local law, or association with a person on the basis on one or more of the foregoing.



Check us out on the web at www.ensafe.com

jobs.title: Associate Water Resources Hydrologist
jobs.description:
**Position Description**
------------------------

  

**Open until filled**  

**Priority Screening:****Thursday, August 27, 2026**
**Exam:** **26/41C14/08GM**  

  

**Associate Water Resources Hydrologist**
$9,332 – $12,746 Monthly  

  

The County of Monterey is committed to honoring the service and sacrifice of veterans and eligible military spouses and awards veterans’ preference points for this recruitment. To learn more about the eligibility requirements and the process, be sure to read the **Hiring Preference for Veterans and Eligible Military Spouses** section located towards the end of this job flier.


The Monterey County Water Resources Agency (MCWRA or Agency) is an independent, special purpose public agency staffed with dedicated employees and focused on water resources management in Monterey County. The Agency was created via a California Water Code Appendix in a statute known as the Monterey County Water Resources Agency Act. The Agency is governed by the Monterey County Water Resources Agency Board of Supervisors for larger policy matters and a nine\-member Board of Directors for more in\-depth oversight.


The Agency provides the following services: control of flood and storm waters, flood warning and monitoring, water conservation, protection of water quality, reclamation of water and the exchange of water. Fundamental to the Agency’s mission to sustainably manage water resources while minimizing impacts from flooding, the MCWRA owns and operates the Nacimiento and San Antonio reservoirs and dams, a hydroelectric facility at Nacimiento Reservoir, the Salinas River Diversion Facility, the Castroville Seawater Intrusion Project, the Salinas Valley Reclamation Project, various drainage facilities, and numerous wells.


MCWRA executes long\-term groundwater and surface water monitoring programs throughout the Salinas Valley Groundwater Basin and provides technical expertise on water resource management and planning throughout Monterey County.


**The Position:**
  

MCWRA seeks qualified candidates to fill two Associate Water Resources Hydrologist vacancies: one in the Operations section and one in the Hydrology and Environmental Resources section.


This position is responsible for supervising assigned program functional activities and professional and technical level personnel. The candidate must perform a variety of complex hydrologic and hydrogeologic assignments and projects that include overseeing aspects of the operations and evaluation of the reservoir release program, flood warning system and other programs related to MCWRA facilities, and the groundwater monitoring program.


The ideal candidates will demonstrate integrity; flexibility and adaptability; be able to navigate complex situations with professionalism and poise; be able to communicate technical and policy information effectively to diverse audiences; and be organized and efficient to complete multiple projects concurrently. This candidate must be able to work collaboratively in a dynamic environment, seek multi\-benefit solutions for new and ongoing projects or programs, and demonstrate good independent judgment.


The ideal candidate for the position in the Operations Section will have a strong background in the operation of water resource\-related facilities such as dams, reservoirs, water diversion structures, or flood conveyance systems; flood warning systems; water rights compliance and reporting; and project and grant management.


The ideal candidate for the position in the Hydrology and Environmental Resources section will have a strong background in groundwater and surface water data collection methodologies, equipment, and industry best practices; data management and monitoring network evaluation; and analysis and reporting of complex datasets.


*The Eligible List established by this recruitment may be used to fill current and future vacancies on a regular full\-time, part\-time, or temporary basis County\-wide.*


**Examples of Duties**
----------------------


**Examples of duties:**
* Supervises and participates in the work of professional hydrology staff responsible for the planning, design, development, operation and maintenance of the department or agency capital improvement projects and programs including flood control, surface and groundwater quality and water supply, storage, treatment and distribution facilities and systems; ensures work quality and adherence to professional codes, standards and department or agency specifications; may provide supervision over assigned maintenance or operations functions.
* Counsels employees, appraises performance, prepares documentation, recommends merit increases, and issues discipline; provides for or participates in employee training and development; conducts interviews and recommends selection of candidates; coaches and mentors subordinate staff.
* Performs the more complex, difficult and large scale hydrologic and hydrogeologic planning, specification, feasibility analysis and calculations for water resources related projects and programs; functions as an expert in assigned area of expertise; prepares conceptual designs and supervises detail design of project phases by other staff and engineers.
* Reviews and evaluates groundwater and surface water supply, availability and/or quality, as well as trends over time; maintains water quality assurance documentation; supervises the operation/evaluation of the Agency’s reservoirs including the conservation release program.
* Oversees the operation and maintenance of water quality, hydrologic, hydrogeologic, land use, well, or groundwater extraction reporting data base; graphs and charts data; prepares maps and reports based on data analysis. presentations

**\#141444 Research Data Analyst 1\- Hybrid**
---------------------------------------------


**Filing Deadline: Thu 10/1/2026**
  

**UC San Diego values and welcomes people from all backgrounds. If you are interested in being part of our team, possess the needed licensure and certifications, and feel that you have most of the qualifications and/or transferable skills for a job opening, we strongly encourage you to apply.**  

  

  

*UCSD Layoff from Career Appointment*: Apply by 9/22/2026 for consideration with preference for rehire. All layoff applicants should contact their Employment Advisor.


*Reassignment Applicants*: Eligible Reassignment clients should contact their Disability Counselor for assistance.


**This position will work a hybrid schedule which includes a combination of working both onsite at Campus and remote.**


**DESCRIPTION**
===============


The Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science is dedicated to creating and promoting public health innovations to advance equity, justice, and wellbeing for all. The School focuses on health, diversity, inclusion, and social equity in everything we do. We believe this starts in the workplace, where we actively strive to ensure a sense of belonging for everyone and honor the idea that through our differences, we are better together. In working to fulfill that vision, we are comprised of more than 125 primary appointed faculty and academics, 150 staff members, and 25 secondary appointed faculty and provide mentorship and instruction to 900\+ BSPH undergraduate major students and 225 postgraduate students across six degree programs as well as a clinical residency. We conduct research and instruction in public health disciplines such as Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, Climate \& Environmental Health, Community Health Services \& Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Behavior, Health Equity \& Justice, Health Policy, Public Mental Health \& Substance Use, and Technology \& Precision Health, totaling \~$255M in grants and contracts and housing five research service cores. We engage in research and teaching collaborations across the University and the community at\-large. Partnerships with the community and with health agencies are fundamental to the School.


The Research Data Analyst possesses basic knowledge of public health, statistics, and data management principles. Under close supervision and guidance from faculty and senior research staff, the Research Data Analyst provides support for research projects by performing routine data management and data quality activities. Responsibilities include maintaining databases, conducting data entry and verification, cleaning datasets according to established procedures, and assisting with data organization and documentation.


The Research Data Analyst assists with compiling data and preparing standard reports, tables, charts, and graphs for research studies. Using established statistical software applications such as SAS, R, Stata, or JMP, the incumbent runs predefined programs and produces routine summaries under direction. The position assists with quality control reviews of data, supports the creation of basic calculated variables, and helps ensure data accuracy and completeness.


The Research Data Analyst conducts literature searches and summarizes findings for research staff, assists with preparing research materials and study documentation, and supports the presentation of research results. The incumbent provides routine assistance to faculty, staff, students, and trainees in locating and accessing research data and resources. Work is performed following established research protocols, procedures, and guidelines, with methods and priorities determined by faculty and senior research personnel.


Under direct supervision, acquires skills and knowledge of professional concepts in research data analysis. Works on small projects or segments of projects with limited scope and complexity.


**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**
==========================


* Four (4\) years of related experience, education/training, OR a Bachelor’s degree in related area.
* Acquiring knowledge of research function. Acquiring ability to perform research analysis duties.
* Acquiring statistical analysis, systems programming, and database design skills to perform research analysis duties.
* Ability to effectively manage time and see assigned parts of projects through to completion on deadline.
* Basic consultation and communication skills.
* Ability to communicate results to scientists and to others. Knowledge of data analysis pipelines that clean, analyze, and output data in ways that are optimized to reduce error and support reproducible science.
* Experience with analysis software such as SAS, R, Stata, and JMP.
* Experience in basic research analysis protocol, results, and conclusion writeups.

**SPECIAL CONDITIONS**
======================


* Employment is subject to a criminal background check.
* Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.

jobs.title: Natural Resources Specialist I/II - Public Works, Clean Water
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**
===============

The Clean Water Division of Clark County Public Works is currently seeking a Natural Resource Specialist I/II. Positions in this class are responsible for performing a variety of field and office assignments to carry out monitoring requirements of Clark County’s NPDES phase I municipal stormwater permit. Work requires the application of standard principles for assessing and evaluating water quality and overall stream health. Duties and activities include applying standard operating procedures over multiple monitoring projects, project management skills that are necessary to successfully complete work assignments, detection and elimination of illicit discharges to the storm system and interacting with the public and outside agencies.
  

  

The primary tasks and responsibilities of this position are to provide technical support for monitoring related activities including water quality and habitat assessments, perform stream discharge measurements, operate and maintain remote logging equipment, and maintain and calibrate multiparameter sondes.
  

  

The Natural Resource Specialist classification is the fully experienced level within the job family. Work assignments are performed with limited technical instruction and require considerable independence in the selection of courses of action and resolution of complex or unique problems within the framework of departmental policy and procedures, applicable regulations, accepted best practices and operating procedures.
  

  

The Public Works department values our community’s diversity and seeks ways to promote equity and inclusion within the organization and with the public. The department encourages applications from candidates with knowledge, ability and experience working with a broad range of individuals and communities with diverse racial, ethnic, and socio\-economic backgrounds.
  

  

This position is represented by Local 307CO \- Washington State Council of County and City Employees.
**Qualifications**
==================

**Education and Experience:**

* Four (4\) year degree with major coursework in a natural science or related field. Two (two) years of experience working in areas related to natural resource science or environmental science.


* On a year‑for‑year basis, any combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted for educational requirements.


**\- AND \-**

Qualified candidates must have a valid driver’s license.


**Knowledge of:** State and local regulations pertaining to water quality and stormwater management; standard operating procedures regarding water quality monitoring; project management related to water quality and habitat assessments; principles, practices and techniques of stormwater management; detection and elimination of illicit discharges; collecting and assessing stream health data.


**Ability to:** Effectively plan and organize work and complete tasks within prescribed timeframes; comprehend, interpret, and implement applicable regulations governing stormwater management and assessing water quality; analyze and evaluate water quality data; independently exercise sound judgment; establish effective working relationships and communication with regulatory agencies, county departments and the public; prepare detailed documentation and communications in the form of written reports, memos, email; maintain a valid driver’s license.


**Selection Process:**

**Resume and other documents must be attached together in the 'Resume Upload' section of the application. Multiple files are allowed, but all applicant attachments must be uploaded simultaneously, as there is no way to edit or append uploaded materials after submitting the application.**

Application Review (Pass/ Fail) \- An online application is required. Attaching a resume does not substitute for a completed application; incomplete applications will not pass the application review. Candidates deemed most qualified will be invited to participate in the remainder of the selection process.


Practical Exam (Pass/Fail) \- This recruitment may require a practical exam which will be job related and may include, but not limited to, the qualifications outlined in the job announcement. Candidates deemed most qualified will be invited to participate in the remainder of the selection process.


Oral Interview \- The interview will be job related and may include, not limited to, the qualifications outlined in the job announcement. Top candidate(s) will continue in the process.


Employment references will be conducted for the final candidates and may include verification of education.


It is general policy of the County that new employees should be hired at the lower steps of the applicable range and advance through the range at the normal progression.


**First review of candidates will be September 30th.** This recruitment may close at any time on or after the first review date with no additional notice.


**Examples of Duties**
======================

**Duties may include but are not limited to the following:**

* Support the work of the Clean Water Division staff and other agencies as it relates to NPDES permit compliance.
* Assists in implementing a variety of environmental monitoring programs and projects.
* Perform water quality, sediment and benthic macroinvertebrate monitoring using established standard operating procedures.
* Operate and maintain remote temperature and stream stage loggers and data recorders.
